objective.statement: Answer questions about intervals, ornaments, directions and instruments in a short passage.
successCriteria: I read the clef, key signature and directions first.
I answer each question with the right rule.
I use what I know of the instrument named in the question.

explanation.text: In the examination, music theory questions often come together in a short piece of music. A single passage may ask about intervals, ornaments, performance directions and the instrument it is written for. Each question uses something you already know; the skill is knowing where to look.

music.textAlternative: An alto stave in D minor, 3/4, marked affettuoso: D, F with a trill sign (marked A), then A below.

explanation.caption: A passage for the viola: alto clef, D minor, marked affettuoso, with a trill on the note marked A.

explanation.text: Method: (1) look at the clef and the key signature: here the alto clef, one flat, D minor. (2) Read the words above the stave: affettuoso, tenderly. (3) Check each sign on the notes: the trill. (4) Think about the instrument: the viola is a string instrument that normally reads the alto clef. Then answer each question on its own, one rule at a time.
Clef, key, words, signs, instrument. Answer each question with the rule that belongs to it.

mastery.completion: The lesson is complete when every step has been answered correctly (retries allowed). Only first-attempt, hint-free independent answers count as mastery evidence; guided steps never do.

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 05, drafted with AI assistance; pending qualified teacher review)
provenance.notes: Original wording and original passages (the book has no passage for this unit; section 15 'General Questions' is the model). The passages are generated, short, written for a named orchestral instrument and combine an instrument question with an interval, an ornament or a performance direction. Every passage carries a question about the instrument, so it is always evidence for the orchestra outcome; the interval, ornament and term parts are counted only by their own templates elsewhere.
